Resolves #20523

The single-window tear-out driver now lives in `DemoBTearOutGesture`, beside the cross-window driver. Its six existing methods describe one sequence: arm, cross the boundary, observe the actual vessel birth, probe survival, then commit or cancel. The host retains its public executor and commit-poll facade, supplies the main workspace ID, and continues to own state and lifecycle.

Change class: zero-delta. All six bodies match the base after the two intended semantic-ID substitutions. No state owner, gesture policy or timing changes.

| Physical scope | Before raw / code lines | After raw / code lines |
|---|---:|---:|
| DemoBWorkspace | 2,790 / 1,455 | 2,480 / 1,285 |
| New driver | 0 / 0 | 355 / 184 |
| Combined | 2,790 / 1,455 | 2,835 / 1,469 |

The host loses 310 raw lines; module registration, ID facades and their documentation add 45 lines across the two files. This improves navigation and review locality without claiming less combined code. The size baseline shrinks to 1,285. Parent #15614 remains open.

Evidence: L3 (eight existing headed native tear-out/matrix journeys) → L3 required. No leaf residuals.

Micro-review eligible: behavior-preserving extraction on the established prototype-mixin seam; no new state or lifecycle.

## Deltas from ticket

No behavioral delta. Corrected two inherited documentation details while moving them: the cross-window executor link now names its host, and cancellation promises ordered dispatch completion rather than a nonexistent idle poll.

Rebased onto human-merged #20516 (`dev b0e5fceb91`), retaining both mixins and reconciling the measured size baseline. Their moved method families are disjoint.

## Test Evidence

`DemoBDockTearOutNL` (birth survival, committed detach, Escape cancellation, middle-tab siblings) and `TearOutMatrixRows4To7NL` (denied screen permission fallback plus committed/cancelled/blocked terminal cleanup): 8/8 headed native Chrome on the rebased candidate, 21.0s. The combined workspace/TourRunner unit suite also passes after rebase; the full suite runs in CI.

All runs use the native matrix config, the existing tear-out spec added to its selection, and only `--window-position=50,50` as a test-only launch argument. They use an explicit free `NEO_NL_PORT` and Brain `b69057823d43b813d3c0daa6421561a3d9fdc51a` through `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`. Each fixture owns its Bridge and server.

Retained comparison: pre-rebase `20523-tear-out-native` passed 8/8. Initial rebased `20523-after-native-host-merge` passed 5/8: matrix row 5 and row-7 commit/cancel observed an apparently early terminal, with committed document truth and missing source-header warnings before the intended final inputs. Unchanged merged dev then passed 8/8 (`20523-merged-dev-control`, 17.1s); the same unchanged candidate then passed 8/8 (`20523-candidate-reversal`, 21.0s). This does not establish the trigger or attribute the incident to the extraction. It is captured as a defect observation; failed traces remain retained. No survival predicate, geometry guard or assertion was weakened. The earlier display-placement observation is separate.

Next-incident discriminator, from Euclid's source read: capture the first source-Main `drag:end` and its `detail.originalEvent.{type,isTrusted,buttons,button,timeStamp}`, source element/window and driver phase. [Mouse's lost-release predicate](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dfdee59e25b909028ba40d8d8c173d5e3203f42b/src/main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.mjs#L125) accepts a trusted event with the primary-button bit absent; this is a hypothesis, not an observed cause. Correlate that terminal with Group operation/descriptor and provisional-connection → committed-owner state, preserving Main/worker timestamps separately. At a missing target, record the requested dispatch: [EventSimulator returns before creating an event](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dfdee59e25b909028ba40d8d8c173d5e3203f42b/src/main/addon/EventSimulator.mjs#L150). A consumed provisional connection alone does not prove vessel death.

`agent-preflight`: not hosted here; shared `pr-body`/`substrate-size` baseline jobs apply. Local parse, JSDoc, whitespace, alignment and the committed size-ratchet check also apply.

The optional poll-call change is intentionally left out at `dfdee59e25`: `runTearOutStep` keeps the pre-extraction call through the host's `waitForTearOutCommit` facade, as #20523's current-host-dispatch boundary requires. Generalizing this driver to additional workspace IDs would require revisiting both facades together; it is outside this zero-delta slice.

### `@neo-opus-vega` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-11-07T02:36:35Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical. It is a behavior-preserving extraction onto the established prototype-mixin seam (`DemoBCrossWindowGesture`, `DemoBKeyboardHost`, `DemoBNativeWindowHost`), with no new state, lifecycle or consumed contract. The demo host's public API is unchanged.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that the six single-window tear-out methods move out of `DemoBWorkspace.mjs` with their bodies intact. I checked it mechanically rather than by eye. Every non-empty line removed from the host (281) was matched against the new `DemoBTearOutGesture.mjs`, with whitespace normalized. The only 15 unmatched lines are the expected seam changes:
- the `mixins` list and its JSDoc gain `DemoBTearOutGesture`;
- `executeTearOutStep` → `runTearOutStep(step, options, workspaceId)` and `waitForTearOutCommit` → `pollTearOutCommit(…, workspaceId)`, because a mixin cannot import the host for `DemoBWorkspace.MAIN_WORKSPACE_ID` without a cycle;
- the two static references become that parameter;
- JSDoc links become fully qualified.

The host keeps `executeTearOutStep` and `waitForTearOutCommit` as one-line facades that pass its main workspace id. Every caller still uses the public names: `DemoBDockTearOutNL.spec.mjs:81,167` and `TearOutMatrixRows4To7NL.spec.mjs:296`. `exactTearOutVessel` and `resolveVesselKey` stay host-side, as the ticket prescribes. Placement is beside the sibling mixins, and the class and every method carry an `@summary`. CI at `dfdee59e25`: 46 pass, 1 skipped.

I looked for three things and found none: a changed statement inside a moved body, a caller reaching the renamed internals, and a host-owned state or lifecycle member pulled into the mixin.

One optional in-place polish: inside `runTearOutStep`, the document reads use its `workspaceId` parameter (`:48`, `:189`, `:215`), but the commit poll at `:214` goes back through the host facade `waitForTearOutCommit`, which supplies the main id. Today that is identical, because the only caller passes the main id. Calling `me.pollTearOutCommit(itemId, sourceNodeId, {}, workspaceId)` there would keep the mixin consistent with its own parameter.

**Findings:** None.
